P8e: Then follow the practical power. Whose name is on the deed? Who's in charge of the housing and the food stores, the vehicles and tools, and any bank account outside the community? Who keeps the records? Who decides who gets admitted, and who picks the reviewers? Who controls access to the kids, or to medicine, and who can make a complaint go away? The org chart might look flat and horizontal, while the keys, passwords, titles and even just general reputation all point to one person.
P12f: Presence of one of these alone isn't proof of abuse, but if several are present, they are worth paying attention to before the founder can explain how the situation is uniquely different in a spiritual way.
P19f: “Your resistance is your wound talking” is pretty much a conversation ender. Once you notice a community diagnosing dissent like this instead of answering it, leave. Better yet, leave before it even gets to the point of people wanting to do group process about your leaving.
P20f: There are some basics that the majority should not be allowed to vote away from any member of a community. These basics include your bodily safety, adequate food and sleep, the right to go to a doctor of your choice, the right to keep your thoughts private, the right to communicate with people outside the community, the right to report harm without asking the accused person's friends for permission, the right to leave. Removing these rights from a community member is not consensual, even if a majority vote does it.
